title: The voltage supplies the energy
spoken: Charge magnitude times voltage magnitude supplies kinetic energy.
explanation: Accelerated from rest through a voltage U, the electron gains energy |q| times U, and all of it is energy of motion. With K = mc²(γ − 1) this fixes the electron's speed.
assumptions: An electron accelerated from rest, then moving at speed v with |v| < c. In section 10 the electron is momentarily at rest in the moving system, so its speed is that system's speed v.
Modern teaching notation: gamma is the paper's beta, |q| the size of the electron's charge, U the size of the voltage.

notes.title: What it asserts
notes.explanation: Energy conservation for acceleration from rest: the work done becomes energy of motion.

notes.title: Charge times voltage
notes.explanation: The work the field does on the electron: coulombs times volts is joules.

notes.title: Size of the electron's charge
notes.explanation: The elementary charge. The sign of the charge decides the direction of the force, not these magnitudes.

notes.title: Kinetic energy
notes.explanation: The electron's energy of motion afterwards: m c squared times gamma minus one, not one half m v squared, which is only its low-speed form.

notes.title: Accelerating voltage
notes.explanation: The voltage the electron falls through, starting from rest.

sentence.text: The size of the electron's charge
